turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I tried running today and I was gasping after one minute. Is something wrong with me?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all, that's really normal when you're starting out. Most beginners go too fast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Can I ask about something else? My car got written off in a hailstorm and the insurance money just came through, so I need a new one fast.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I'm torn between— no, let me just describe every option and you can comment after.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My uncle's selling his estate car, it's high mileage but he's looked after it really carefully.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: There's a nearly new small crossover at the dealer in town, with a warranty, but it eats most of the payout.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I could also buy a cheap runaround for now and keep the rest of the money in savings.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Alright, I'm finished. What's your opinion?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: I'd lean towards the uncle's car if the service history checks out. The dealer crossover gives you peace of mind at a high price, and the runaround is only worth it if you plan to upgrade soon.
